transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Time: 16:00 - 16:42 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sam Park (Redwood AE), Nina Shah (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Redwood CSM), Elena Cruz (CTO, Aurora), Marcus Li (SRE, Aurora), Derek Zhao (Head of ML, Aurora), Priya Nair (Security Lead, Aurora)

Summary:
Quick follow-up to the postmortem we shared after last week's incident where production inference latency spiked and some requests errored for ~35 minutes. Review of proposed mitigations, validation plan, and next steps to avoid recurrence. Discussed KV cache eviction behavior, autoscaler tuning, and observability gaps (trace sampling, token-level logging). Agreed on a staged validation path and a timeline for pilot patch.

Topics covered:
- Root cause recap (KV cache pressure + fallback hot path causing degraded kernels)
- Immediate mitigations implemented (threshold tuning + temporary routing change)
- Long-term fixes: kernel upgrade, improved TTLs for caching, stronger circuit-breakers, more aggressive prefix caching for common prompts
- Observability improvements: add token-level metrics, increase trace sampling during high tail latency, better alerting thresholds
- Security/compliance notes: audit logs, KMS integration for private key material, SOC2 scoping for patch changes
- Validation plan and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Sam Park: hey everybody, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, we're on for 40 minutes, follow-up to the incident postmortem we circulated, i'm Sam from Redwood, with Nina and Ravi. Elena, Marcus, Derek, Priya from Aurora, thanks for making time.

[00:18] Elena Cruz: yeah thanks sam, appreciate it. we read the postmortem, good level of detail, just want to make sure we're aligned on the immediate and long term fixes and we need clear dates for our compliance team.

[00:35] Nina Shah: quick recap, the short version is we saw an unexpected KV-cache eviction cascade when a few large multi-shot prompts hit the runtime, that caused the runtime to fall back to a slower kernel path and the autoscaler to spin new workers, which increased tail latency and a portion of requests hit 5xx before the steady state returned.

[00:58] Marcus Li: yeah i still have the traces open, it looks like the cache eviction window overlapped with our batch size burst, so the memory churn was higher than expected. some of the product names in the logs are a bit mangled \"Redwood Private\" and then \"redwood-ded,\" transcription is weird - but the stack was the hosted runtime hitting fallback paths.

[01:20] Derek Zhao: can you clarify the difference between the fallback kernel and a normal execution path, i want to make sure our model team understands impact on logits and determinism?

[01:30] Nina Shah: great q. the fallback kernel uses a more conservative attention implementation when KV cache is disabled or out of memory; it trades throughput for memory-safety. results are functionally equivalent but you can see slight latency jitter and, in rare cases, tokenization timing differences which can change beam ordering in heavy sampling. not a model correctness bug, more an execution performance tradeoff.

[02:05] Elena Cruz: ok so this is not a correctness/regression, but performance. still, customers saw errors - what's the error mode? 502? 503?

[02:14] Nina Shah: predominantly 503/timeouts and some internal 500s when the process exceeded internal watchdog thresholds. the autoscaler also delayed provision by ~30s in that window.

[02:33] Ravi Menon: to clarify what we changed immediately after detection, we lowered the eviction aggressiveness, bumped the prefix cache retention for the top 50 prompts Aurora uses, and temporarily routed critical traffic to a reserved pool while we triaged. that cut the tail significantly.

[02:55] Marcus Li: that routing change helped. we confirmed latency dropped to normal for the routed traffic. but we need a permanent fix before we can turn off the reserved route.

[03:10] Elena Cruz: timeline question - how long to a proper kernel update or runtime patch? and what are the risk/rollback steps?

[03:20] Nina Shah: kernel upgrade is a 2-week dev + 1-week staging validation typically; for this patch specifically, we've got a smaller mitigation - adjusting cache TTL heuristics + a more aggressive circuit breaker - that we can roll in ~72 hours for staging validation and then a 1-week canary in prod. risk is low, rollback is instant: flip the routing policy back and revert TTL changes.

[03:48] Priya Nair: from security/compliance perspective, any change that touches cache or tracing could affect PII handling. we need to ensure audit logs are intact and that the cache doesn't store sensitive payloads unencrypted. does the patch touch KMS or storage layers?

[04:05] Nina Shah: good point. this patch is purely runtime heuristics and circuit-breaker logic, it doesn't change KMS or storage. we'll add an explicit filter to ensure keys and PII patterns are excluded from cache and add a note to the postmortem.

[04:25] Derek Zhao: i'd like to see the perf delta for model outputs when the fallback kernel is used - could we include a small regen test comparing probabilities for a sample suite?

[04:36] Nina Shah: absolutely, we'll run a regen and include token-probability diffs and end-to-end latency numbers. that will be part of the staging run.

[04:50] Sam Park: also want to address the observability gaps we saw. trace sampling was at 0.1% during the incident so we missed a lot of contextual info. we propose a dynamic sampling increase when latency SLOs are breached and to ship token-level counters for queues and cache hits/misses.

[05:12] Marcus Li: yes that would've helped. i can share our trace configuration; can you also add a high-cardinality metric for request shape (seq len + batch size) so we can pivot on the right dimension?

[05:26] Nina Shah: good call, we'll add that metric. it will be in the observability PR.

[05:35] Elena Cruz: SLA impact - we saw 7 minutes of degraded error rate in our dashboards, what's Redwood's position on credits?

[05:45] Ravi Menon: i'll open the credit request and include the incident timeline. based on the SLA terms, we'll evaluate and propose credits; i'll share the case id and the proposed credit by 2026-12-03.

[06:00] Priya Nair: i'll need an updated attestation for SOC2 changes if the mitigation requires any infra changes beyond runtime. please flag early.

[06:10] Sam Park: will do, we'll flag the compliance team if anything touches persistent storage or KMS.

[06:20] Derek Zhao: about the KV-cache behavior - is there a way we can preload or pin prefixes for our top flows to avoid eviction spikes?

[06:30] Nina Shah: yes, we added a prefix-pin feature in the immediate mitigation; longer term we can expose a policy where you pin top-N prompts or set soft-residency for known warm prefixes. that will be part of the product roadmap if Aurora wants it.

[06:50] Elena Cruz: we do want that - our call volume pattern has a heavy tail of a few dozen prompts that are critical. pinning would help. what about costs? pinning increases memory use and could bump cost for dedicated pools.

[07:05] Sam Park: correct, there's a tradeoff; our Optimize team can run a model-level cost-impact analysis. Nina, can you include a rough estimate for memory delta and cost delta for pinned prefixes?

[07:16] Nina Shah: yes we'll include numbers in the benchmark sheet.

[07:25] Marcus Li: concrete ask - during the follow-up bench run can we run a simulated burst with larger seq lengths and mixed batch sizes, same as production traffic last Friday, to validate?

[07:38] Nina Shah: yep that's the plan for the staging run. we'll coordinate on traffic replay, need request traces from Aurora to make it realistic.

[07:50] Marcus Li: i'll export a sanitized trace set and share a link in the doc.

[08:02] Ravi Menon: on the communications front, customers asked for a clearer timeline; can we commit to dates?

[08:10] Sam Park: commit to draft postmortem by 2026-12-01, staging patch in ~72 hours after that, bench run week of 2026-12-06, canary week of 2026-12-13, follow-up 2026-12-14.

[08:28] Elena Cruz: ok that's reasonable. Priya - any security blockers for that timeline?

[08:35] Priya Nair: just need to review the patch notes and validate that no PII touches the cache; assuming that's in the doc we can do a fast review. if any storage or KMS changes are needed, that pushes timeline.

[08:50] Nina Shah: to be explicit about mitigations: (1) heuristic change to cache TTLs and eviction thresholds, (2) circuit-breaker to short-circuit requests when queue length > X, (3) prefix pinning for top-N prompts, (4) dynamic trace sampling and token-level metrics. only (1) and (2) in the immediate patch.

[09:15] Derek Zhao: can you explain the circuit-breaker thresholds - what's X and what's the behavior?

[09:22] Nina Shah: X is currently configurable; for Aurora we propose queue_length > 500 triggers 429 backpressure to client, and the router will route to reserved pool or return a synchronous 429 depending on policy. default is 500 but we can tune.

[09:42] Marcus Li: 429 sounds ok if it's synchronous; our current client retries are exponential and that could create thundering herd - we need clear guidance on retry jitter and client-side backoff.

[09:55] Sam Park: we'll produce a client guidance note in the runbook: recommended retry policy, jitter, and idempotency considerations.

[10:05] Elena Cruz: audit and postmortem - we need the full event timeline with timestamps and traces, plus the list of requests that failed and sample payloads redacted. can you provide?

[10:18] Ravi Menon: yes we'll attach the timeline and sanitized request samples to the postmortem doc. Marcus, please share any additional traces.

[10:28] Marcus Li: will do. i'll sanitize and upload to the shared folder.

[10:36] Nina Shah: action item for us: we'll also add a section on regression detection - add a synthetic check that hits top-N prefixes every 10s and an alert if latency rises above 95th pct.

[10:50] Derek Zhao: for model team, we'll also run a small experiment to compare output distributions between normal kernel and fallback kernel to ensure no downstream drift for our prompting pipeline.

[11:05] Sam Park: on the business side, if Aurora wants to move to Dedicated or Private to avoid noisy neighbors and get more predictable memory behavior, we can scope that, but that's a separate sales conversation. today is about reliability and quick mitigations.

[11:28] Elena Cruz: note that Dedicated has compliance advantages for us, but procurement will need clear TCO and migration plan. not part of this immediate patch but flagging it.

[11:40] Priya Nair: and for audit scope, if we migrate to Private we need KMS integration and a security assessment.

[11:50] Sam Park: understood. we'll keep that as an action separate from the incident follow-up.

[12:00] Nina Shah: final items - we'll include the perf workbook with expected memory footprint delta for prefix pinning, the regen tests for token-prob diffs, and the trace sampling changes. expect PRs and docs by 2026-12-01.

[12:18] Elena Cruz: thanks everyone. if we can get the postmortem and the runbook quickly i can present it to our execs.

[12:28] Sam Park: thank you, we'll get the draft out. recap of next steps in the doc.

[12:35] Ravi Menon: i'll create the SLA credit case and share it.

[12:40] Derek Zhao: thanks all.

[12:42] Meeting end.
